messages:
jamie.ops: quick q — on-call just asked me to run `kubectl exec` into a prod pod for a live debug. before i do anything, can someone confirm the exact approval steps and redaction checklist? not sure if i should request a temp role or open a short approval ticket.

maria-sec: short answer: follow the runbook section 'prod access' — require on-call + manager sign-off via #sec-approvals, and create a short-purpose incident/JIRA with start/end times and scope. no permanent role grants. use ephemeral creds (STS/session) and enable session recording if available. :lock:

leo-sre: +1. operational notes: avoid interactive root on hosts. prefer `kubectl exec -it pod -- /bin/sh -c "..."` for non-root tasks, and if you need root ask SRE to run the command (we can grant single-command sudo). do not paste raw logs with PII into slack.

nguyen-eng: quick question — if i need to pull a file with `kubectl cp`, do we need an approved storage destination, or can i scp from the bastion to my laptop?

maria-sec: `kubectl cp` is allowed but files must land in an access-monitored, ephemeral bucket or privileged S3 path. never copy PHI/PII to a local laptop without DLP/approval. if the file potentially contains secrets, request a DLP scan first. for most cases, prefer `kubectl logs --since=1h | sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+.[A-Za-z]{2,}/[REDACTED_EMAIL]/g'` to sanitize before sharing.

jamie.ops: runbook mentions `sudo -i` is discouraged — what is the practice if i need to run a privileged command quickly?

leo-sre: correct — no interactive root unless SRE coordinates. workflow: open the ticket, include exact command lines you need, and request SRE oncall to execute them. we can also provision a one-off `sudo` for a single command (session recorded) or use `sudo -u root -S -- bash -lc '...your command...'` under audit.

sev-bot: INCIDENT BOT: Access request created #sec-req-4823 by jamie.ops. Approval pending: maria-sec, leo-sre.

jamie.ops: thanks — i'll open the ticket with the exact `kubectl` commands, the short justification, and include the redaction steps. i'll wait for approval before touching prod.

maria-sec: copying runbook excerpt link: https://redwood/ops/runbooks/prod-access — checklist: approval thread, ephemeral creds, session recording, do not paste PII, DLP if needed, rotate any tokens used, and add a post-debug note.

nguyen-eng: one more nit — if you need to capture env vars or config that might include tokens, mask them with `<TOKEN_REDACTED>` in the ticket and rotate immediately after.

leo-sre: yep. after debug, rotate creds if any token was exposed, close the ticket, and tag artifacts with `sensitive:delete` if they should be removed. also add a brief postmortem if the access was non-trivial.

jamie.ops: done — ticket created, pinging @maria-sec and @leo-sre for approvals. will not exec until approved. :white_check_mark:
